meta.purpose: Map analytical intent and data shape to chart type, and flag documented anti-patterns. Consulted after the design plan declares an intent and the data schema is known, and again against the rendered SVG.

perceptual_basis.citation: Cleveland, W. S., & McGill, R. (1984). Graphical Perception: Theory, Experimentation, and Application to the Development of Graphical Methods. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 79(387), 531-554.
perceptual_basis.note: Lower rank = more accurate quantitative decoding. Chart selection means choosing the mark whose primary channel sits at the lowest feasible rank for the declared intent.

intent_to_chart.comparison: grouped/sorted bar (position on common scale); dot plot for many categories
intent_to_chart.trend_over_time: line chart (ordered x = time); connected scatter or slope chart for few points
intent_to_chart.distribution: histogram or density for one variable; box plot (Tukey, EDA 1977) or violin for group comparison; strip/beeswarm for small n
intent_to_chart.part_to_whole: stacked bar for one-to-few totals; treemap only for hierarchy overview; pie only for 2-3 slices of one whole
intent_to_chart.relationship: scatter plot (two quantitative); binned heatmap for high n; add trend line for correlation
intent_to_chart.ranking: sorted horizontal bar or dot plot, ordered by value
intent_to_chart.flow: Sankey (Sankey 1898, band width proportional to flow magnitude); alluvial for categorical transitions; chord for symmetric flows
intent_to_chart.uncertainty: error bars, confidence bands, or gradient/fan for a mean or estimate; do not present an estimate as a bare point/line without its interval

rules.principle: Match the mark type to the declared analytical intent using the intent-to-chart map before any styling.
rules.applies_when: The design plan states an intent (comparison, trend, distribution, part-to-whole, relationship, ranking, flow, uncertainty) and a mark.type.

check.detail: Look up plan.intent in meta.intent_to_chart and confirm plan.mark.type is among the recommended types for that intent; flag any pairing not listed (e.g. intent=distribution with mark.type=pie).

rules.fix: Replace the mark with the first recommended type for the declared intent, or correct the stated intent if the mark is deliberate.

rules.principle: For comparison or ranking of magnitudes across categories, encode value as bar length or dot position on a common zero-based scale, not as angle or area.
rules.applies_when: Intent is comparison or ranking over one quantitative value across nominal categories.

check.detail: Flag if mark.type is in {pie, donut, arc, bubble, packed-circle, treemap} while intent is comparison|ranking. On SVG, arc <path> segments or <circle> sized by the compared field are violations.

rules.fix: Switch to a sorted bar or dot plot on a shared axis; reserve angle/area encodings for rough overviews only.

rules.principle: For trend over time, use a line chart with time on an ordered x-axis; do not use an unordered or categorical layout for temporal data.
rules.applies_when: The data has a temporal or otherwise ordinal x field and intent is trend_over_time.

check.detail: Confirm the x field type is temporal|ordinal and its scale preserves natural order; flag mark.type=bar for a dense continuous time series, and flag any reordering of time (e.g. sorted by value) on the x-axis.

rules.fix: Use a line (or connected scatter for sparse points) with time sorted ascending on x; use bars over time only for a small number of discrete periods.

rules.principle: For a single-variable distribution, use a histogram, density, or box/violin plot, never a bar chart of raw unaggregated rows.
rules.applies_when: Intent is distribution and the plan encodes the spread or shape of one quantitative variable.

check.detail: For intent=distribution confirm the variable is aggregated into bins/quantiles (histogram binCount present, or box-plot summary stats) rather than one mark per raw row; flag a plain category bar of un-binned values.

rules.fix: Bin the variable (histogram/density) or summarize it (box/violin) so shape, center, and spread are visible; use box or violin when comparing distributions across groups.

rules.principle: For a relationship between two quantitative variables, use a scatter plot; switch to a binned or 2D-density heatmap when overplotting hides structure.
rules.applies_when: Intent is relationship over two quantitative fields.

check.detail: Confirm mark.type is point|scatter|heatmap for two quantitative encodings. Flag when point count exceeds a density threshold (e.g. >2000 marks) with no binning/opacity strategy declared in the plan.

rules.fix: Use a scatter for moderate n; for large n add alpha, 2D binning, or hexbin/density so the joint distribution is legible.

rules.principle: Reserve part-to-whole charts (pie, stacked, treemap) for when the parts genuinely sum to a meaningful whole, and cap pie/donut at two or three slices.
rules.applies_when: Intent is part_to_whole, or mark.type is pie|donut|stacked-bar|treemap.

check.detail: Confirm parts sum to 100% of one whole (values non-negative, mutually exclusive). Flag pie/donut with more than 3 slices, and flag part-to-whole marks whose values do not sum to the stated total.

rules.fix: For more than 3 parts use a sorted bar (comparison) or a single stacked bar (composition); ensure parts are exhaustive and non-overlapping, or relabel the intent.

rules.principle: Use a Sankey or alluvial diagram for flow between stages, with band width strictly proportional to flow magnitude and conserved across each node.
rules.applies_when: Intent is flow, or data is source-target-value triples describing transfers between nodes/stages.

check.detail: Confirm mark.type is sankey|alluvial|chord for flow data. On SVG, sum of inbound band widths equals sum of outbound at each node (within tolerance); flag non-conserving or non-proportional band widths.

rules.fix: Encode each link's value as band width on one scale and balance flows per node; if magnitudes are not conserved, use a network/arc diagram instead.

rules.principle: Show uncertainty explicitly: any plotted estimate, mean, or forecast must carry its interval (error bar, CI band, or fan), never appear as a bare point or line.
rules.applies_when: The plan plots an estimated, sampled, modeled, or forecast quantity and the data or plan carries a variance/CI/std field.

check.detail: When a field is marked estimate|mean|forecast and an uncertainty field exists in the data, confirm the plan renders an error bar, band, or interval mark; flag its absence.

rules.fix: Add error bars or a confidence band from the available uncertainty field; if no uncertainty is quantified, annotate the estimate as a point estimate without implied precision.

rules.principle: Never plot two unrelated series on a dual y-axis, because arbitrary axis scaling manufactures apparent correlation.
rules.applies_when: The plan defines two independent quantitative y-scales (secondary axis) for two series.

check.detail: Flag the presence of a secondary y-axis / independent second y-scale in the plan. On SVG, two distinct y-axis tick groups with different domains bound to different series.

rules.fix: Split into small multiples with aligned time axes, index both series to a common base (e.g. =100 at t0), or plot the relationship directly as a scatter.

rules.principle: Do not render faux-3D, exploded, or perspective versions of any chart; depth distorts the length/area the reader must decode.
rules.applies_when: The plan or renderer requests 3d, isometric, extruded, exploded, or perspective marks on 2D data.

check.detail: Flag if mark.type or style contains 3d|extrude|explode|perspective|isometric. On SVG, offset duplicate polygons or depth gradients simulating volume.

rules.fix: Render the flat 2D form of the chart and remove all depth/explosion effects.

rules.principle: When one comparison must be split across categories, prefer small multiples with a shared scale over a single overloaded chart with many overlapping series.
rules.applies_when: The plan overlays many series (roughly >5) of the same measure on one set of axes, or intent is comparison across a facetable dimension.

check.detail: On the rendered SVG, check whether individual series are separable or collapse into a spaghetti tangle; overlapping indistinguishable lines/areas indicate faceting is warranted.

rules.fix: Facet into small multiples with an identical shared axis domain per panel; optionally highlight one series against a muted background set.

rules.principle: Choose the color-scale family to match the data type: sequential single-hue for ordered magnitude, diverging for a meaningful midpoint, categorical only for nominal groups.
rules.applies_when: A field is encoded to color as a primary or secondary channel (heatmap, choropleth, category color).

check.detail: Confirm scale family matches field type: quantitative->sequential (e.g. Blues, Viridis); quantitative-with-midpoint->diverging (e.g. RdBu, BrBG); nominal->categorical. Flag a categorical/rainbow scale on a quantitative field or a sequential scale on nominal categories.

rules.fix: Swap to the matching palette family (ColorBrewer sequential/diverging for ordered data, a categorical set for nominal); never encode order with rainbow hue.

rules.principle: Sort categorical axes by value for comparison and ranking; keep the natural order only for inherently ordinal or temporal categories.
rules.applies_when: Intent is comparison or ranking over a nominal categorical axis.

check.detail: For intent=comparison|ranking with a nominal category axis, confirm the axis is sorted by the encoded value; flag alphabetical or arbitrary order. Exempt fields typed ordinal|temporal, which must keep natural order.

rules.fix: Sort the category axis by the plotted value (descending for ranking); preserve natural sequence only for ordinal or time categories.

rules.principle: Verify the chosen chart's focal comparison is visually resolvable in the render, not merely correct in the plan.
rules.applies_when: Any final chart before delivery, once an SVG is rendered.

check.detail: On the rendered SVG, confirm the reader can perform the intended decode: the key comparison stands out, marks do not fully occlude one another, and the primary quantity is read from the highest-accuracy channel present rather than an ambiguous one.

rules.fix: Adjust encoding, ordering, opacity, or faceting so the declared primary comparison is the most legible relationship in the figure.
